rationale: The reversal-long thesis has stalled — price was rejected at $24.30 (the prior short's invalidation) on the heaviest candle since entry, has now broken the 24.26–24.29 consolidation on rising down-volume, and sits below the 9-EMA at 24.26 with MFE of just 0.08% after ten minutes. With only 42 minutes to close, the path to the $24.68 target is impaired while the $24.14 stop remains live, so flattening at roughly breakeven (bid $24.26 vs. $24.27 entry) is the cheapest way to eliminate that risk. Flipping short is not justified: a six-cent micro-breakdown is not meaningfully stronger than flat when it means fighting a risk-on tape (SPY +0.94%, sentiment 0.93) for a ~9-cent target into the thrice-tested 24.15–24.17 shelf.
